$comment: arcnow.io shared curve test vectors, SCHEMA 2: the version-2 CONSTANT-PRODUCT curve.
GENERATED - do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: forge script script/GenerateVectors.s.sol
WHICH CURVE THIS IS. Every row prices a BondingCurve whose VERSION() is
arcnow/bonding-curve at major version 2: the constant-product curve, and the only
one arcnow.io supports. There are no linear (version 1) vectors. A curve at any
other major version is not priced by these rows: refuse it rather than guess.
Produced by contracts/test/vectors/VectorSet.sol through the very CurveMath and
CurveQuote a live BondingCurve settles with. contracts/test/vectors/Vectors.t.sol
asserts this file still matches those libraries, and VectorsOnChain.t.sol replays
every state's history through a real deployed curve and requires the same numbers.
EVERY AMOUNT IS AN EXACT 18-DECIMAL INTEGER ENCODED AS A DECIMAL STRING. Parse them
with BigInt, never Number. USDC is 18 decimals here (native USDC on Arc); the USDC
ERC-20 predeploy reports 6 and is a factor of 1e12 away. Prices are wad USDC per
wad token.
MATCHING IS EXACT, TO THE WEI. There are no transcendentals in version 2: every
function is integer multiply and divide, and k = r0Wad * y0Wad must be formed at
512 bits (it exceeds 2^128). The mathRows section evaluates each function on a curve
with k = 21; agree with it before attempting the rest.
THE CURVE, IN INTEGERS. Y = y0Wad - tokensSold. C(Y) = ceil(r0Wad * y0Wad / Y), the
USDC reserve the curve holds at Y. Buy with net USDC d: Y' = ceil(k / (C(Y) + d)),
tokensOut = min(Y - Y', tokens left for sale). Sell t tokens: gross = C(Y) - C(Y + t),
fee on gross. Spot price = floor(C(Y) * 1e18 / Y). A curve's position is Y, never its
stored reserve: above 1 USDC per token a buy can leave the stored reserve a few wei
above C(Y), and that surplus stays in the curve (see the above-one-usdc template).
ROUNDING RULE: every rounding favours the CURVE. Both reserves are ceiled, the spot
price floored, both trade fees ceiled. A port that rounds the other way is not
slightly wrong, it is drainable in a loop.
THE PURE QUOTE IS NOT THE WHOLE CONTRACT. A live BondingCurve rejects a zero amount
with ZeroAmount, refuses every trade once graduated() is true, and requires a seller
to hold the tokens. So the zero-amount rows quote to zero here and revert on chain,
and every 'graduated' state is priceable here and untradeable there.

units.usdc: native USDC, 18 decimals - NOT the 6-decimal ERC-20 predeploy

identities: Checks a port can run against every row. Y' = y0Wad - newTokensSoldWad, and
C(Y) = ceil(r0Wad * y0Wad / Y), with the row's template's r0Wad and y0Wad:
newReserveWad    >= C(Y'), and == on every template priced below 1 USDC/token
For a buy, amountInWad is gross USDC offered and amountOutWad is tokens delivered.
For a sell, amountInWad is tokens offered and amountOutWad is USDC paid out net of
fee. refundWad and usdcSpentWad are zero on a sell, and a sell never graduates.

helpers.$comment: feeUp(x) = ceil(x * tradeFeeBps / 10000). grossForNetUp(x) = ceil(x * 10000 / (10000 - tradeFeeBps)), the smallest gross whose net after feeUp is at least x. Both round UP, in the curve's favour.

templatesComment: Each template as PlatformConfig stores it, what it derives to, and its shape: the spot price after a fee-free buy of each fraction of its target into a fresh curve. The multipliers at the same progress agree across templates to one part in 1e12 - the curve's shape does not depend on its target.

templates.note: arcnow.io's reference template, ArcConstants REFERENCE_*: 1e9 tokens, a 50,000 USDC target, the 14.312x multiplier kept from version 1.
The Arc testnet platform, ArcConstants TESTNET_*: the reference shape at a thousandth of the supply and of the target, so every price equals the reference.
1e9 tokens and a 1,000,000 USDC target at the reference multiplier, derived by test/support/CpmmTemplate.sol. Same multipliers at the same progress as reference.

1e6 tokens and a 1,000,000 USDC target: priced above 1 USDC per token, the only regime in which a buy can leave the stored reserve a few wei above C(Y). A port that prices from the stored reserve instead of from Y disagrees here first.

mathRowsComment: Each CurveMath function evaluated exactly. argWad is the reserve argument (the token reserve Y, or the USDC reserve V for tokenReserveAt); amountWad is the trade amount, zero for the reserve functions. The first rows use r0 = 3, y0 = 7, so k = 21 and C(Y) for Y = 1..7 is 21, 11, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3.

states.note: A curve nobody has traded: reserve r0, nothing sold, Y = y0, and the spot price is floor(r0 * 1e18 / y0).
One buy of target/50000 gross (1 USDC on the reference template): small enough that the fee and the ceilings are visible.
One buy of a fifth of the target, gross.
Traded both ways: a buy of two fifths of the target, then a fifth of the tokens it bought sold back.
One buy of four fifths of the target, gross.
Net target/50000 short of graduation. The graduation crossing lives here.

A fifth of the target bought and every token it bought sold straight back. Below 1 USDC per token this is exactly the fresh state again, reserve r0 to the wei: sells telescope and a round trip neither creates nor destroys USDC before fees. Above it, any surplus a buy left in the reserve stays in the curve.

Four times the target offered: capped, refunded, graduated. Priceable - the cap is zero, so every buy refunds in full and buys nothing - but NOT tradeable: a live curve here reverts on every buy, sell and quote.

launchVectorsComment: ILaunchpad.quoteLaunch(initialBuyWad) on the reference template. totalCostWad is the exact msg.value launch() requires: launchFeeWad + initialBuyWad. The initial buy is an ORDINARY buy against a fresh curve and pays the ordinary trade fee on top of the flat launch fee.
